issue: Can a district court reduce, under § 404 of the First Step Act, the sentence for a non-covered offense that was packaged with the sentence for a covered crack offense?

sides.position: Yes. A court may reduce a non-covered sentence that was packaged with a covered sentence under the sentencing-package doctrine.
cases: United States v. Richardson, 96 F.4th 659 (4th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Hudson, 967 F.3d 605 (7th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Gordon, Nos. 23-1050/1069/1070/1071 (6th Cir. 2025)

sides.position: No. The First Step Act lets a court reduce only the sentence for the covered offense, and the sentencing-package doctrine does not supply the express statutory authority needed to modify a sentence.
cases: United States v. Young, 998 F.3d 43 (2d Cir. 2021)
United States v. Gladney, 44 F.4th 1253 (10th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Baptiste, 834 F. App'x 547 (11th Cir. 2020)

this_court: The Sixth Circuit adopts the sentencing-package interpretation, finding the reasoning of the courts permitting such reductions more persuasive, and remands to decide whether the doctrine applies on these facts.
quote: Although some circuits disagree on this issue, we find the reasoning of courts adopting a sentencing-package interpretation more persuasive.
cite: United States v. John Gordon, No. 23-1070 (6th Cir. 2025)
